verses.text: Yahweh is my shepherd: I shall lack nothing.
He makes me lie down in green pastures. He leads me beside still waters.
He restores my soul. He guides me in the paths of righteousness for his name’s sake.
Even though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil, for you are with me. Your rod and your staff, they comfort me.
You prepare a table before me in the presence of my enemies. You anoint my head with oil. My cup runs over.
Surely goodness and loving kindness shall follow me all the days of my life, and I will dwell in Yahweh’s house forever.

1.title: Accompanied Through the Shadowed Valley
1.historicalBackground: Attributed to David, who spent his youth tending flocks across the limestone hills and steep wadis of Judea, Psalm 23 draws on concrete pastoral realism rather than idyllic sentimentality.
1.theologicalContext: Notice the intimate shift in pronouns halfway through the psalm. Verses 1–3 speak about God in the third person ("He makes me lie down," "He leads me"), but the moment the path enters the dark canyon in verse 4, the poet turns directly to God: "You are with me." Crisis strips away distant theology and invites direct address.
1.practicalApplication: If anxiety keeps your mind racing, note verse 2: "He makes me lie down." Rest is not laziness; it is an act of trust under a faithful Shepherd’s watch.
1.reflectionPrayer: Faithful Shepherd, calm my anxious thoughts beside your still waters. When I walk through shadowed valleys today, remind me that your rod and staff are near, and let your steadfast mercy surround my steps. Amen.

In the Judean wilderness, green pastures are rare pockets of seasonal grass, and "still waters" (mei menuchot) are calm pools built or cleared by a shepherd because sheep will not drink from rushing torrents.

lyrics.title: Still Waters, Steadfast Guide
verse1: In quiet meadows washed in gold,
Where rushing rivers learn to rest,
You call my weary heart to breathe
And lay its burden on Your chest.
chorus: Though shadows lengthen down the stone,
I will not walk this path alone;
Your rod and staff are comfort here,
My Shepherd keeps me close and near.
verse2: Before my doubts You set a feast,
With mercy poured until it spills;
Across the valleys and the hills.
bridge: Mercy holds me in its grace;
Home at last within Your house,

verses.text: He who dwells in the secret place of the Most High will rest in the shadow of the Almighty.
I will say of Yahweh, “He is my refuge and my fortress; my God, in whom I trust.”
He will cover you with his feathers. Under his wings you will take refuge. His faithfulness is your shield and rampart.
You shall not be afraid of the terror by night, nor of the arrow that flies by day;
For he will put his angels in charge of you, to guard you in all your ways.

1.title: Dwelling in the Secret Shelter
1.historicalBackground: Psalm 91 combines architectural images of a fortified citadel with the tender shelter of a mother bird’s outstretched wings.
1.theologicalContext: Safety in the Psalms begins with "dwelling" (yashav)—remaining close to God before crisis strikes, rather than visiting only in emergencies.
1.practicalApplication: Before sleep tonight, speak verse 2 aloud as a quiet boundary against fear: "You are my refuge and my fortress."
1.reflectionPrayer: Most High God, cover my household tonight beneath your faithful wings and quiet every anxious alarm. Amen.

lyrics.title: Shadow of the Almighty
verse1: In the presence of Most High.
chorus: My shield through day and night;
verse2: Every step is watched and kept
In the mercies You have told.
bridge: I will rest, I will trust,
You are faithful, You are just.
